row.evidence: Concord offers SAML SSO configured "at your company account level" and SSO users on an approved domain "will be automatically assigned as a user in your Concord account and given a seat"; no SCIM is documented.
row.notes: None by absence (medium): pricing page, help-centre sitemap (185 articles), the OpenAPI spec and the SSO guides mention no SCIM. Automation is SAML JIT: users on an approved domain get a seat on first sign-in. Prices are flat per plan with 5 users included (Essentials $499/mo, Business $899/mo, Enterprise $1299/mo, paid annually; extra users $49/$69/$89 per month), so per-user fields stay null. Which plan includes SSO could not be read: the comparison table's check icons render client-side and the headless renderer was blocked. The REST API (Open API, Enterprise on the pricing cards) can list members, invite users and manage user groups but cannot remove users.

scim.notes: No SCIM endpoint or IdP provisioning app is documented. SSO is SAML (Okta, OneLogin, Azure AD, Google, ADFS) configured by Concord's onboarding team; users with an approved domain are created on first sign-in.

endpoints.purpose: Bulk update user groups with users and invitations

limitations.text: No API endpoint to remove, deactivate or change the role of an organization member was found in the spec; removal is done in Users Settings.

okta.notes: okta.com/integrations/concord/, /concordnow/ and /concord-now/ returned 404; Concord documents a custom SAML app for Okta.

entra.notes: Concord's Azure guide uses a non-gallery app ('Integrate any other application you don't find in the Gallery'); learn.microsoft.com concord-tutorial 404.

fallbacks.notes: Users invited by email (comma-separated list) in Users Settings. With SSO, anyone on an approved domain is auto-assigned a seat on first sign-in unless access is restricted by IdP group assignment. Removing a user frees the seat (except Viewers).
